# Libraries
```{r}
# spatial data science
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(units)

# Data
library(AOI)

# Visualization
library(flextable)
library(gghighlight)
library(ggrepel)
library(knitr)
```

# Question 1
```{r}
# Define projection
eqdc <- '+proj=eqdc +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-96 +lat_1=20 +lat_2=60 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs'

# 1.2 - Get USA state boundaries and reproject
states <- aoi_get(state = 'conus') %>%
  st_transform(crs = eqdc)

# 1.3 - Get country boundaries (USA, Mexico, Canada) and reproject
countries <- aoi_get(country = c("MX", "CA", "USA")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = eqdc)

# 1.4 - Read city CSV and make it spatial
cities_raw <- read_csv("data/us_cities.csv")

# Convert to sf object
cities <- st_as_sf(cities_raw,
                   coords = c("lng", "lat"), # Make sure these are the correct column names
                   crs = 4326) %>% # Original is in WGS84
  st_transform(crs = eqdc)

# Filter for cities in the lower 48 states
cities <- cities %>%
  filter(state_id %in% unique(states$state_abbr))
```


# Question 2
```{r}
# Turn state boundaries into a single dissolved shape and convert to border lines
us_border <- states %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_cast("MULTILINESTRING")

# Calculate distance from each city to the US border (in km)
cities$dist_to_border_km <- set_units(st_distance(cities, us_border), "km") %>% drop_units()

# 5 cities farthest from US border
border_ft <- cities %>%
  select(city, state_name, dist_to_border_km) %>%
  arrange(desc(dist_to_border_km)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  flextable()

```
```{r}
# Preserve all state borders (no dissolve)
state_borders <- states %>%
  st_union(by_feature = TRUE) %>% # keep individual states
  st_combine() %>%
  st_cast("MULTILINESTRING")

# Calculate distance to nearest state border
cities$dist_to_state_km <- set_units(st_distance(cities, state_borders), "km") %>% drop_units()

# 5 cities farthest from state borders
state_ft <- cities %>%
  select(city, state_name, dist_to_state_km) %>%
  arrange(desc(dist_to_state_km)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  flextable()

```
```{r}
# Extract and cast Mexico border
mexico_border <- countries %>%
  filter(admin == "Mexico") %>%
  st_cast("MULTILINESTRING")

# Distance to Mexico
cities$dist_to_mexico_km <- set_units(st_distance(cities, mexico_border), "km") %>% drop_units()

# 5 cities farthest from Mexico
mexico_ft <- cities %>%
  select(city, state_name, dist_to_mexico_km) %>%
  arrange(desc(dist_to_mexico_km)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  flextable()

```
```{r}
# Extract and cast Canada border
canada_border <- countries %>%
  filter(admin == "Canada") %>%
  st_cast("MULTILINESTRING")

# Distance to Canada
cities$dist_to_canada_km <- set_units(st_distance(cities, canada_border), "km") %>% drop_units()

# 5 cities farthest from Canada
canada_ft <- cities %>%
  select(city, state_name, dist_to_canada_km) %>%
  arrange(desc(dist_to_canada_km)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  flextable()

```

# Question 3
```{r}
# Get top 10 most populous cities
top10_cities <- cities %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  slice(1:10)

# Base map
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "gray90", color = "black", size = 0.4) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "darkgray", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_sf(data = top10_cities, aes(size = population), color = "blue") +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = top10_cities,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3,
    color = "black",
    box.padding = 0.3,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Most Populous Cities in the USA",
    subtitle = "With National and State Boundaries",
    size = "Population"
  )

```

```{r}
# Get 5 cities farthest from the national border
farthest_us_border <- cities %>%
  arrange(desc(dist_us_border_km)) %>%
  slice(1:5)

# Map
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "gray90", color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray50", linetype = "dotted", size = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = cities, aes(color = dist_us_border_km), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Distance (km)", option = "magma") +
  geom_sf(data = farthest_us_border, color = "red", size = 1.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = farthest_us_border,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3,
    box.padding = 0.4,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distance of U.S. Cities from the National Border",
    subtitle = "Cities colored by their distance (km) from any U.S. border",
    color = "Distance from Border (km)"
  )

```

```{r}
# Get 5 cities farthest from the nearest state border
farthest_state_border <- cities %>%

```

```{r}
# Create a new column with absolute distance difference
cities <- cities %>%
  mutate(dist_diff_mc = abs(dist_canada_km - dist_mexico_km))

# Filter cities in equidistance zone (±100 km)
equidistant_cities <- cities %>%
  filter(dist_diff_mc <= 100)

# Get 5 most populous cities in this zone
top5_equidistant <- equidistant_cities %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  slice(1:5)

# Map
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "gray95", color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray60", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = equidistant_cities, aes(color = dist_diff_mc), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Distance Difference (km)", option = "magma", direction = -1) +
  geom_sf(data = top5_equidistant, color = "red", size = 2) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = top5_equidistant,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Cities Equidistant (±100 km) from Mexico and Canada",
    subtitle = "Top 5 most populous cities in this zone highlighted",
    color = "Distance Difference"
  )

```

# Question 4
```{r}
# Cities within 100 miles (~160 km) of a US border
border_zone <- cities %>%
  filter(dist_border_km <= 160)

# Total US city population
total_population <- sum(cities$population, na.rm = TRUE)

# Total population in border zone
border_population <- sum(border_zone$population, na.rm = TRUE)

# Percent of population in border zone
border_percentage <- (border_population / total_population) * 100

# Summary table
border_summary <- tibble(
  `Number of Cities` = nrow(border_zone),
  `Population in Zone` = border_population,
  `Total Population` = total_population,
  `Percent of US City Population (%)` = round(border_percentage, 1)
)

# Show as flextable
flextable::flextable(border_summary)

```

```{r}
# Get top 10 most populous cities in the border zone
top10_border_zone <- border_zone %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  slice(1:10)

# Map
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "gray95", color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray60", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = border_zone, aes(color = population), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkred", name = "City Population") +
  geom_sf(data = top10_border_zone, color = "blue", size = 2) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = top10_border_zone,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Cities within 160 km of the U.S. Border",
    subtitle = "Top 10 most populous cities in the Danger Zone",
    color = "Population"
  )

```

```{r}
# Find most populous city per state within the border zone
most_populous_per_state <- border_zone %>%
  group_by(state_name) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = population, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Map
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "gray95", color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray60", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = border_zone, aes(color = population), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkred", name = "City Population") +
  geom_sf(data = most_populous_per_state, color = "blue", size = 2) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = most_populous_per_state,
    aes(label = city, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 3,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Most Populous Cities in Each State within 160 km of Border",
    subtitle = "One city per state in the Danger Zone",
    color = "Population"
  )

```
